canon_status.description: Canon posture. Canonical enum values only. Use 'canon_status_description' for prose context (e.g., 'post-Fate of the Jedi, 47 ABY').

canon_status_description.description: Optional descriptive phrase elaborating on the canon_status. Use for era/divergence context.

tone.description: Primary tonal register. Use 'tone_description' for descriptive blends that don't fit the enum neatly.

tone_description.description: Optional descriptive phrase elaborating on the tone (e.g., 'Classic Star Wars adventure layered over genuine moral dilemma — personal stakes, tight cast, archaeological mystery building to cosmic crisis').

series.description: Reference to series seed (for planned_series or continuation)

protagonist_arc_type.description: Top-level classification of the protagonist's arc. Per-character structured arc classification lives under ensemble_cast[].weiland_arc.arc_type.

voice_notes.description: Per-character voice guidance. Deprecated in favour of voice_definition.character_voices (post-Phase-5); retained for backward compatibility with Phase 5 seeds.

arc_type.description: Weiland arc type — canonical enum only. Use 'arc_summary' for the descriptive phrase.

arc_summary.description: Optional descriptive phrase elaborating on the arc (e.g., 'moves from the lie (self-reliance as safety) to the truth (collective trust as strength)'). Complements the strict arc_type enum.

initial_phase.description: The arc phase this character starts the story in. Defaults to 'lie_established' for all arc types. Must be a valid phase for the character's arc_type.

arc_phase_map.description: Chapter-level map of Weiland arc progression. Keys are phase names (e.g., lie_established, lie_reinforced, lie_challenged, moment_of_truth, new_truth_demonstrated, arc_resolved). Tragic and flat arcs may use variant names (e.g., lie_deepened, point_of_no_return, lie_tested, lie_unchanged). Values are chapter references. Optional — supporting characters with minor arcs may omit this.

referenced_characters.description: Characters who appear in scene cards but are not in the ensemble cast. Registered with minimal state (no arc tracking). Franchise-agnostic way to prevent 'unknown character' warnings.

voice_definition.description: Narrative voice identity for the book. Produced by Step 5 of the concept workshop.

reference_authors.description: Authors whose prose the book emulates. Each entry is an object with guidance on what to emulate and what to avoid.

character_voices.description: Per-character voice guidance, keyed by character name. Each value is a free-form description of how the character speaks and thinks.

anti_slop_rules.description: Flat list of slop-avoidance rules. Replaces the legacy nested anti_slop.{banned_words, banned_phrases} structure.

anti_patterns.description: Structural anti-patterns to avoid (e.g., 'no prophecy fulfillment structure').

force_description_guidelines.description: Optional — genre-specific phenomenological rules for describing magic, the Force, or other setting-specific systems.

info_id.description: Legacy alias for revelation_id. Accepted for backward compatibility.

content.description: Legacy alias for 'what'. Accepted for backward compatibility.

revealed_in.description: Chapter where this is revealed. Accepts integer or string reference.

revealed_chapter.description: Legacy alias for revealed_in (integer only). Accepted for backward compatibility.

items.description: Each entry must supply either 'term' (canonical form) or 'canonical_form' (workshop-style). Both are accepted for compatibility with different workshop outputs.

first_appearance.description: Chapter of first appearance. Accepts either an integer chapter number or a string reference like 'Chapter 1' or 'Chapter 5 (First Plot Point)'.

stress_test_scores.description: 9-dimension stress test scores. Produced by Step 10 of the concept workshop.

subplots.description: Subplot list. Each entry describes a subplot arc with an ID, name, narrative function, summary, and the chapters across which it is active.

hooks.description: Hook list. Each entry describes a narrative hook with an ID, type (hard/soft/series), plant and payoff chapters, and a description of the reader contract.

planted_in.description: Chapter where the hook is planted. Accepts either integer or string form.

resolved_in.description: Chapter where the hook is resolved (or 'next_book' for series hooks).

scene_cards.description: Workshop-format scene cards. These are plan-level artifacts produced by Step 8 of the concept workshop. Individual drafting-level scene card files (matching schemas/scene_card.json) are extracted from this list into data/story_bibles/{project}/scene_cards/.

promise_payoff_ledger.description: High-level reader-promises tracked across the book. Complements the hook map — hooks are plot-mechanic contracts, promises are thematic/character-level reader expectations that may span multiple beats. Populated during Step 7 or as a post-stress-test enrichment.

related_hook_id.description: Optional cross-reference to a hook in the hooks array that shares this promise's reader contract.

quality_overrides.description: Per-project overrides for quality metric thresholds. Prevents franchise-specific false positives (e.g., 'Force' flagged as overused in Star Wars).

word_frequency_allowlist.description: Words that should not be flagged as overused. Case-insensitive.

semantic_similarity_threshold.description: Cosine similarity above which paragraph pairs are flagged. Default: 0.85.

max_similar_pairs_per_1k_words.description: Maximum similar paragraph pairs per 1000 words before triggering alert.

canon_profile.description: Franchise canon and continuity profile for the canon expert agent. All specialization for canon validation comes from this section — the agent code contains zero franchise-specific content.

franchise.description: The franchise or world this story belongs to. Use 'original' for original fiction.

continuity.description: Which continuity or canon tier applies. For original worlds, use 'primary'.

continuity_description.description: Human-readable explanation of the continuity scope — what counts as valid source material and what doesn't.

era_description.description: When this story is set within the franchise timeline, including key context about the state of the world.

narrative_register.description: The expected prose tone and voice — space opera, grimdark medieval, literary fantasy, hard sci-fi, etc.

cross_continuity_violations.description: Specific terms, characters, or concepts from OTHER continuities that should be flagged if they appear.

anachronistic_terms.description: Real-world terms that break the franchise voice, mapped to their in-universe replacements.

meta_reference_rules.description: Out-of-universe reference systems or fan terminology that should never appear in prose.

franchise_terminology_notes.description: Any additional franchise-specific voice or terminology guidance.

extended_metadata.description: Container for project-specific structural data that doesn't belong in the universal schema. Examples: technique_lineage (Star Wars Legends), jacen_parallel, workshop_origin. Arbitrary sub-fields are permitted.
